title: Stopmotion
review: Strangely for a horror movie, this is a normal setting with realistic characters, but it's tense right from the start. We don't learn about the characters in a relaxed state, and so we don't get the dynamic emotions from seeing their situation deteriorate from normality. I wasn't rooting for anyone and didn't know what the stakes were. I also thought the writing was a bit lame. I can't really explain why, but I felt like the characters talked and behaved like they were in a cheap horror movie, and not like they were humans who lived on Earth. It makes sense that a stop-motion solo project would look basic and rugged, and the best parts for me were the scenes where she quietly works on her project, but it would have been much cooler if the animation was really good. Imagine an edit of this film where the actual stop motion footage she's making is for {Wallace & Gromit}. Imagine if the villain was an overbearing Wes Anderson trying to micromanage every aspect of {Fantastic Mr. Fox}, and the protagonist was just a cog in a huge machine, tasked only with moving Mr. Badger's toenails.
